Saruman: Saruman the White was the first and greatest of the Istari and head of the White Council. Seeking the Ring for himself, he turned to Sauron's cause, ruled Isengard and bred the Uruk-hai, and was overthrown by the Ents and the Rohirrim.
Radagast: Radagast the Brown was an Istar who lived at Rhosgobel on the edge of Mirkwood. He cared more for beasts and birds than for the affairs of Elves and Men, and Gandalf asked him to send the creatures of the Wild to bring word of Saruman's doings.
Alatar: Alatar was one of the two Blue Wizards, the Ithryn Luin, who came to Middle-earth with the other Istari and journeyed into the East. Tolkien's notes leave their fate uncertain.
Pallando: Pallando was one of the two Blue Wizards, the Ithryn Luin, who came to Middle-earth with the other Istari and journeyed into the East. Tolkien's notes leave their fate uncertain.
Witch-king of Angmar: The Witch-king of Angmar was the chief of the Nazgûl, a Man corrupted by one of the Nine Rings. He ruled Angmar in the north, destroyed the kingdom of Arthedain, and led Sauron's armies against Minas Tirith until Éowyn and Merry brought him down.
Mouth of Sauron: The Mouth of Sauron was the Lieutenant of Barad-dûr, a Black Númenórean who had forgotten his own name. He met the Captains of the West at the Black Gate and showed them Frodo's mithril coat.
Valar: The Valar were the Powers of Arda, Ainur who entered the world at its making to shape it and prepare it for the Children of Ilúvatar. Manwë was their king, and they dwelt in Valinor.
Maiar: The Maiar were lesser Ainur who served the Valar. Gandalf and the other Wizards, Melian, Sauron and the Balrogs were all Maiar.
Ents: Ents were the Shepherds of the Trees, ancient tree-like beings of Fangorn Forest and among the oldest peoples of Middle-earth. They were made to protect the forests, and in the War of the Ring they marched on Isengard.
Treebeard: Treebeard, called Fangorn in the Elvish tongue, was the eldest of the Ents. He took Merry and Pippin under his care and led the Ents against Isengard.
Huorns: Huorns were tree-like beings, thought to be Ents or trees that had grown wild and awake. At Helm's Deep they came in the night and destroyed Saruman's Orc host.
Eagles: The Great Eagles were intelligent birds of great size who served Manwë and watched over Middle-earth. They rescued Thorin's Company from the Wargs and Frodo and Sam from Mount Doom.
Gwaihir: Gwaihir, the Windlord, was lord of the Great Eagles of the Misty Mountains. He rescued Gandalf from Orthanc and from Zirakzigil, and carried Frodo and Sam from Mount Doom.
Thorondor: Thorondor was King of the Eagles in the First Age. He rescued Maedhros from Thangorodrim and bore away Fingolfin's body after his duel with Morgoth.
Beorn: Beorn was a skin-changer who lived in a wooden hall near the Carrock and took the shape of a great bear. He sheltered Thorin's Company and fought in the Battle of the Five Armies.
Drúedain: The Drúedain, also called the Woses or Wild Men of the Woods, were a squat, ancient people of the forests. In the War of the Ring they showed the Rohirrim a hidden path to Minas Tirith.
Orcs: Orcs were foul creatures bred by Morgoth, of uncertain origin. They served Morgoth, then Sauron and Saruman, and made war on every free people.
Uruk-hai: The Uruk-hai were a stronger breed of Orc that appeared in the Third Age. Those bred by Saruman could march in sunlight, and a band of them took Merry and Pippin at Amon Hen.
Goblins: Goblin is another name for Orc, used for the Orcs of the Misty Mountains in The Hobbit. Their Great Goblin ruled beneath the mountains and captured Thorin's Company.
Azog: Azog was an Orc chieftain who killed Thrór at the gate of Moria in T.A. 2799 and sparked the War of the Dwarves and Orcs. In the books Dáin Ironfoot slew him at Azanulbizar; in the Hobbit films he survives to hunt Thorin.
Bolg: Bolg was Azog's son and led the Orcs of the North at the Battle of the Five Armies, where Beorn killed him.
Uglúk: Uglúk was a captain of the Uruk-hai of Isengard who led the band that carried Merry and Pippin toward Isengard. Éomer killed him.
Shagrat: Shagrat was the captain of the Tower of Cirith Ungol. After a fight with Gorbag over Frodo's mithril coat, he carried it to Barad-dûr.
Trolls: Trolls were huge, strong creatures made by Morgoth in mockery of Ents. Most turned to stone in sunlight until Sauron bred the Olog-hai.
Stone-trolls: Stone-trolls were Trolls who turned to stone in sunlight. In The Hobbit, Bert, Tom and William are caught this way when Gandalf keeps them arguing until dawn.
Olog-hai: The Olog-hai were a stronger, cunning breed of Troll bred by Sauron late in the Third Age. They could endure sunlight while his will was upon them.
Cave-trolls: Cave-trolls were Trolls of the deep places. One attacked the Fellowship in the Chamber of Mazarbul in Moria.
Balrog: Balrogs were Maiar of fire corrupted by Morgoth, wreathed in flame and shadow and wielding whips of fire. Most perished in the War of Wrath, but one remained in Khazad-dûm.
Durin's Bane: Durin's Bane was the Balrog awakened beneath Khazad-dûm in T.A. 1980 when the Dwarves delved too deep for mithril. Gandalf fought it on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm and the two fell into the abyss.
Dragons: Dragons were fire-breathing worms bred by Morgoth, among the mightiest of his creatures. They hoarded treasure and brought down kingdoms.
Smaug: Smaug was the last great dragon of Middle-earth. He took the Lonely Mountain from the Dwarves of Erebor in T.A. 2770 and was slain by Bard of Lake-town in T.A. 2941.
Glaurung: Glaurung was the first of the dragons, called the Father of Dragons. He burned Nargothrond and put spells on Túrin and Nienor, and Túrin slew him at Cabed-en-Aras.
Ancalagon the Black: Ancalagon the Black was the greatest of the winged dragons. He was cast down in the War of Wrath, and his fall broke the towers of Thangorodrim.
Scatha: Scatha the Worm was a dragon of the Withered Heath who troubled the Northmen. Fram, son of Frumgar, slew him and took his hoard.
Wargs: Wargs were evil wolves of the Wild that hunted with Orcs and rode to war with them. They hunted Gandalf and Thorin's Company in The Hobbit.
Werewolf: Werewolves were evil spirits in wolf-shape, sent by Sauron in the First Age. Draugluin was their lord at Tol-in-Gaurhoth.
Carcharoth: Carcharoth, the Wolf of Angband, was a huge wolf who guarded Morgoth's gate. He bit off Beren's hand as it held a Silmaril, and was driven mad by its burning.
Fell beasts: Fell beasts were great winged creatures that the Nazgûl rode after the Ring was found. A fell beast carried the Witch-king into the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.
Ungoliant: Ungoliant was a vast spider-spirit of darkness who devoured the light of the Two Trees with Morgoth. Her offspring included Shelob.
Shelob: Shelob was a giant spider who lived at Cirith Ungol, the last child of Ungoliant. She stung Frodo, and Sam drove her off with Sting.
Spiders: The spiders of Mirkwood were huge spiders of the Forest, kin to Shelob. They caught Thorin's Company, and Bilbo rescued the Dwarves with the help of Sting.
Nazgûl: The Nazgûl, or Ringwraiths, were nine Men corrupted by the Nine Rings and bound to Sauron's will. They hunted the Ring-bearer, led by the Witch-king.
Barrow-wights: Barrow-wights were evil spirits sent by the Witch-king of Angmar to haunt the Barrow-downs. One caught the hobbits, and Tom Bombadil rescued them.
Dead Men of Dunharrow: The Dead Men of Dunharrow were Men of the White Mountains who broke their oath to Isildur and were cursed to remain undead. Aragorn called them to fight at Pelargir and then released them.
Watcher in the Water: The Watcher in the Water was a tentacled creature that lived in the lake before the West-gate of Moria. It seized Frodo, and the Fellowship fled inside.
Mûmakil: Mûmakil, or Oliphaunts, were huge elephant-like beasts that the Haradrim used as war-beasts. They fought at the Pelennor Fields, where the Rohirrim brought them down.
Crebain: Crebain were large crows from Dunland and Fangorn that Saruman used as spies. The Fellowship hid from them near Hollin.
